x: Jack Brown, the holder, was a non-starter, but a small bunch of runners soon detached themselves from the rest of the field with Lucas, Herbert, Tooby, Bromley, Stokell, Bruce and Stearman more or less together.

John Bromley handed over in third place on the first " leg " and then Arthur Bruce took us into the lead with a really fine run and he did the fastest time of our team and indeed the third fastest of the afternoon.
Herbert, Bruce, in 7th place, our "D" team of—Ken Stimpson, Bolam, Stace, Len Bishop, were 16th and our "E" team—R. Mitchell, Cuff, Tween, Porter, 22nd out of the 30 clubs that closed in.
Arthur Bruce pulled us up three places on the 2nd stage and Chas. Walker brought us to 5th on the third leg, and we then ran Jack Braughton in an endeavour to overhaul the leaders.
Times of all our runners were as under :— " A "—Walker, 23.33 ; Bromley, 23.54 ; Bruce, 24.37 ; L.
Dave Baulch running the next leg, also did a Club best time beating by 10 seconds the three year old time of Bruce, which was a course record in those days.
Ron Hayes backed up very well indeed for 9th and with Hurd, Keyes and Bruce packing well in the late 'teens we were assured of second place in the team event.
Pearson, Coy and Stow and a 'B' (medium) pack led by Messrs. Bruce, Biscoe and Mead. Provision will be made for a 'C' (slow) pack as the occasion arises.

Apart from the normal over-indulgences, Go Kart racing resulted in a most spectacular crash involving Bruce Barton and his Cross Country Team Manager (poor Bruce was unable to run for weeks) while the exploits on the golf course saw a Belgravian on an adjacent fairway struck on the rump by a Belgrav…
